did_you_know.text: Did you know? Proverbs warns us not to envy evil people or desire to join them, because their hearts plot violence and their lips speak trouble.
Did you know? According to this chapter, a house is built by wisdom, established by understanding, and filled with precious treasures through knowledge.
Did you know? The proverb presents many advisers as a source of strategy, success in battle, and victory: sound plans depend on wise counsel.
Did you know? Wisdom is beyond the fool’s reach, so he does not open his mouth at the gate—the place of discussion and judgment.
Did you know? This verse teaches that losing heart in the day of trouble reveals how limited a person’s strength is; hardship tests perseverance and resilience.
Did you know? The chapter places a responsibility on us to rescue people being led to death or slaughter, rather than avoiding action by claiming that we did not know.
Did you know? Even if someone says, “I did not know,” the verse emphasizes that the Lord examines the heart, knows and watches over every life, and repays each person according to his deeds.
Did you know? The sweetness of honey serves as a picture of wisdom: just as honey is good and sweet to the taste, wisdom is good for the soul and brings a future and hope.
Did you know? The verse describes the righteous person as one who falls seven times and rises again, unlike the wicked, who stumble into ruin.
Did you know? The lazy person’s field and vineyard provide a practical lesson: thorns, weeds, and a broken wall show that neglect and excessive idleness lead to poverty.
